title: Target (in play only for performance)
body: The numeric target a performance requirement must meet. It carries an `availableWhen` gate — `kind == performance` — so it is in play only for performance requirements and shows as not-applicable ('—') for every other kind. This is category-driven reshaping: the primary `kind` choice decides which fields exist for a record, evaluated server-side and sent to the client.

title: Serves (the means-end link / the 5 whys)
body: The parent intention this one is a means toward — grounded as HQDM `part_of_plan`. Following `serves` upward is the 5-whys: model-driven collaboration → many authors build reliably → intent survives the building → intent is faithfully realized. The intention with no `serves` is the FIRST intention; everything else is in service of it.

title: Criterion (built from the choices)
body: The acceptance predicate BUILT from the choices (comparator, observable, target) by the `build` op — a first-class, deferred predicate value, not prose. Authored once here; the very same object is what runs at verification. This is why a requirement is a configurator: it computes its own criterion.

title: Satisfying observations
body: How many Observations of this requirement satisfy its criterion (a rollup of observations.metNum). The requirement is a `requirement_specification` — a CLASS of satisfying states — so 'is it met?' is 'does any observed state fall inside the class?'. metCount > 0 is the runtime gate for verification.

title: Observation — evidence as an individual state
body: A measured state of the world offered against a requirement. An HQDM `state` (an individual, a temporal part), distinct from the requirement it is classified against. It carries the `measured` value; the requirement carries the spec. Splitting them fixes the level error of putting evidence on the spec-class.

title: met — the classification, computed at runtime
body: 1 when this observation's `measured` value satisfies its requirement's criterion, else 0. It runs the requirement's built predicate — `check(requirement.criterionExpr, measured)` via a cross-record ref — so `met` is the HQDM classification relation evaluated live: is this individual state a member of the requirement_specification? 'Done' is a predicate that RUNS.

title: Status + the verification seam (an event)
body: draft → accepted → verified. The move accepted → verified is a GATED TRANSITION grounded as an HQDM `event` — the boundary between two temporal-part states of the requirement — whose guard is `metCount > 0`: a requirement can only become verified once some Observation satisfies its criterion. The WorkspaceDO refuses the move fail-closed before persisting; the op-log entry (at, actor) is the event's point_in_time and party.
